extraction_scope: worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology repair from primary XML/PDF, Fig. 1 peptide design, Fig. 2 fusion inhibition, and Fig. 3 CD analysis.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: HR2 peptides P1/P4/P6 and HR1 peptides N46/N46eg from SARS-CoV spike protein
mechanism_claims.claim_text: The reported peptides inhibit SARS-CoV entry at the membrane-fusion step by targeting HR1/HR2 six-helix-bundle formation rather than by direct antimicrobial killing.
mechanism_claims.direct_assay_type: S protein-mediated cell fusion inhibition assay; SARS-CoV infectivity assay for P1/P4/P6

source_locator.locator: xml:abstract/results/discussion plus Fig. 3 CD analysis caption

mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper does not report direct binding constants or membrane permeabilization assays; mechanism is supported by fusion/infectivity assays and HR1/HR2 structural rationale.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: P1/N46, P6/N46, and P1/N46eg peptide combinations
mechanism_claims.claim_text: CD spectra show secondary-structure changes for HR1/HR2 peptide complexes, supporting complex formation as biophysical context for fusion inhibition.

source_locator.locator: Fig. 3 CD spectra; caption in source/paper.xml xml:fig=3

mechanism_claims.limitations: CD figure is not digitized into exact quantitative curve values; it supports secondary-structure context only.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: N46 plus N46eg at 1:1 molar ratio
mechanism_claims.claim_text: N46 plus N46eg shows synergistic fusion inhibition with a reported combination index of 0.75 ± 0.15.
mechanism_claims.direct_assay_type: S protein-mediated cell fusion inhibition assay with combination-index analysis

source_locator.locator: xml:results paragraphs linked to Fig. 2D/E; pdf_text/main.txt mirrored snippets

mechanism_claims.limitations: The source reports combination index and dose-reduction indices, but not a separate direct target-binding assay.

unsupported_mechanism_claims: No primary-source support for membrane permeabilization or antimicrobial killing mechanism was found in this paper.
